description: Machine-readable recovery guidance for EPER/DX. Pair with catalog.json for status/title/doc anchors. Never capture secrets.

entries.fix: Use a trimmed ASCII dot-atom address such as user@example.com.; Remove display/header control characters. Use Address::named() only with a normal display name.
Read the concrete error message and correct that message field before sending.; Do not retry unchanged invalid input.
Use a fully-qualified domain such as example.com or mail.example.com.; Remove schemes, paths, underscores, spaces, and leading/trailing hyphens from DNS labels.
Validate the selected provider transport, sender identity, region/domain and credentials.; Use provider API credentials for API transports and provider SMTP credentials for SMTP transports.
Pass an absolute provider-local path beginning with one /, for example /emails.; Do not pass full URLs to provider-native request_json().
Use a method supported by both the provider endpoint and the RBE net:http broker.
Supply the provider credential through authorized RBE configuration; never hard-code it in source.; For SMTP, use SMTP credentials when the provider distinguishes them from API keys.
No recovery guidance until emitted.
Pass the verified Mailgun sending domain only, not a URL/path.
Pass only the domain registered/verified in SendPulse.
Use an AWS region identifier such as ap-south-1 and ensure the SES identity exists in that region.
Use a valid legacy template id only when the upstream SendGrid legacy-template feature is still appropriate.
Use the provider-documented SMTP hostname and port.; Prefer STARTTLS/TLS profiles and never downgrade to plaintext to bypass MAIL2004/MAIL4010.
Open the provider SMTP settings and use its documented SMTP username/password/token pair.
Pass a fully-qualified public domain such as gmail.com.
Keep untrusted/user text in the body. Validate/encode structured header values before passing them to mail.
Use simple variable names such as first_name or order-id.
Use setup_records_with_token() with valid example.com / mail.example.com names, a public IPv4 address, and a secure verification token.

Generate 32 cryptographically random bytes outside the package and pass their 64-character hex encoding to setup_records_with_token().; Do not derive ownership tokens from timestamps, domains, counters or user ids.
Use the publicly routable IPv4 address that will actually receive SMTP for mail.<domain>.; If you need IPv6-only setup, use a future AAAA/ip6-aware setup surface rather than lying in an A/ip4 record.
Use RFC-style Message-IDs such as <opaque-id@example.com>.; Pass References as whitespace-separated Message-IDs only.
For RFC 8058 one-click, use an HTTPS unsubscribe URI.; For non-one-click List-Unsubscribe, https:// or mailto: is accepted by this helper.
Keep product/code at 128 characters or fewer and expiry between 1 and 1440 minutes.; HTML is escaped automatically; do not pre-inject markup into product/code.
Inspect the package approval/grant state and approve the required capability when RBE supports it.; Reactivate/restart the package session after grants change.
Call self_hosted_capabilities() and enable every missing prerequisite.; Use a provider transport until current RBE supplies the missing package-host primitives.
Do not bypass RBE with std::net/raw sockets. Use provider HTTP mode until RBE net:tcp is implemented and granted.
Never downgrade to plaintext SMTP. Use provider HTTPS mode or wait for RBE TLS authority.
Approve net:dns for mail and reactivate the package session.
Execute the component through RBE/RPX package activation, not as a standalone binary.; Check SDK ABI/session logs if the package should already be hosted.
Generate 32 random bytes with a trusted CSPRNG outside the package and call setup_records_with_token() with 64 hex characters.; Do not fall back to timestamp-derived tokens.
Verify/rotate the provider credential and sender/domain permissions.; Do not retry unchanged credentials.
Honor Retry-After/provider backoff semantics and reduce request concurrency.

entries.whatFailed: Provider quota or billing limit reached
entries.fix: Fix provider billing/quota/account state before retrying.
Inspect provider-detail and correct the rejected field/policy before retrying.
Retry with exponential backoff, or deliberately switch provider if your application supports that policy.
Treat delivery as ambiguous: query provider/idempotency state before resending.; Use an idempotency key where the provider supports it.
Inspect the underlying RBE broker diagnostic (HTTP3000/DNS3000/etc.).; Retry only if the failed operation is known to be safe/idempotent.

entries.whatFailed: RBE request or response limit exceeded
entries.fix: Reduce/split message, attachment or provider request data so it fits the active RBE broker limits.; Do not blindly retry the same oversized payload.
No recovery guidance until emitted.
Do not send plaintext. Use provider HTTPS mode until RBE TLS/STARTTLS is implemented/granted.
Enable the RBE package listener primitive when implemented; keep server mode disabled meanwhile.
Use provider-only mode until RBE can register/activate package-owned mail.service.
Check the recipient/domain DNS externally and inspect the underlying DNS3000 detail.; Retry transient DNS failures with backoff.

entries.whatFailed: No mail exchanger or address fallback
entries.fix: Correct the recipient domain/address. This is not fixed by retrying the same invalid domain.
Do not retry. Correct the recipient/domain or use another contact address.
Install/restore the prerequisite named in the error and rerun build.ps1/build.sh.

entries.whatFailed: Latest green RBE commit could not be resolved
entries.fix: Check GitHub access or set GITHUB_TOKEN.; Pass -RbeSha/--rbe-sha with a known-green full SHA as an explicit fallback.

entries.whatFailed: RBE source checkout or backend build failed
entries.fix: Read the underlying Git/RBE compiler output.; Delete .cache/rbe/upstream to refresh a corrupt checkout and retry.

entries.whatFailed: RBE SDK bootstrap or status failed
entries.fix: Inspect backend install/sdk status output and repair/reinstall .rbe.; If CLI syntax changed upstream, compare against backend install help.

entries.whatFailed: RPX validation or package compilation failed
entries.fix: Fix the first compiler/RPX/RBE diagnostic printed above MAIL5005 and rerun.; Use host-toolchain escape hatch only for deliberate local development when no managed toolchain exists.
Preserve the sanitized raw detail, package version and RBE commit; report compatibility drift.; Do not guess status/success when required metadata is malformed.
Preserve the DNS response/RBE version and report the incompatibility.; Do not proceed to SMTP with malformed MX data.
Report the code, MailError::diagnostic(), package version and RBE commit with a minimal reproducer.
Correct the host clock/time synchronization and retry.; For SES, also ensure clock skew is within AWS signing tolerance.
